notifications.templates.help_params:
Variables (placeholders) this notification type supports — declared in the template's params_schema.

HOW TO USE:
1. Click a chip (e.g. {{user_name}}) → the string `{{user_name}}` is inserted into the Body field of the currently open tab.
2. Place placeholders anywhere inside Title/Body, repeat as needed: "Hi {{user_name}}, your order {{order_code}} is…".
3. At send time, backend substitutes each {{param}} with the real value for that recipient/event (e.g. {{user_name}} → "John Doe").
4. Red chips (required) MUST be passed by the emitter; gray chips (optional) can be skipped — missing ones render as empty string.
5. The PREVIEW panel on the right uses sample values <param_name> so you can visualize the rendered output.

notifications.templates.help_params_requ: REQUIRED variable — emitter MUST pass this when firing the event; otherwise backend logs a warning and substitutes empty string. Convention: lowercase snake_case (e.g. user_name, order_code) or dotted (e.g. user.name) — invalid characters auto-replaced with underscore.
notifications.templates.help_params_opti: OPTIONAL variable — emitter may omit; missing values render as empty string (no warning). Use for auxiliary fields like nickname, extra notes…

settings.order.payment_policy_descriptio: Applies to takeaway orders (customer-web / kiosk). Controls whether the kitchen starts cooking immediately or waits for payment.

settings.order.payment_policy_help:
Applies to EVERY takeaway order — card-prepaid (Stripe) included. Dine-in and POS counter orders always go straight to the kitchen and are unaffected.

• Follow HQ: inherit the brand default (system-wide default is 'require payment before prep').
• Require payment before prep: the order is created as confirmed — the kitchen can't see it. Only once the cashier collects full payment does the workstation print the kitchen ticket. Safer for high-value items.
• Start prep immediately: the order is created as open — it hits KDS and prints the kitchen ticket the moment it's placed; payment is collected later. Faster service but risky if the customer walks.
settings.order.payment_policy_on_help:
Takeaway orders are created with status=confirmed → hidden from KDS, and the workstation does NOT print a kitchen ticket.

Once the cashier collects full payment on POS the order moves to closed and the workstation automatically prints the kitchen ticket + receipt together — no extra confirm step. The kitchen is driven by the printed ticket, not KDS (a paid order is no longer in the KDS list), so this mode needs a kitchen printer.

At-counter orders carry a payment deadline (15 min by default, configurable per brand/branch) — unpaid past it, the order is auto-cancelled.

The customer mail subject is 'Order #XXX has been placed' with the order QR to show the cashier.
settings.order.payment_policy_off_help:
Takeaway orders are created with status=open → they show on KDS right away and the workstation prints the kitchen ticket on arrival. No POS confirm needed.

No payment deadline is set → the order is NEVER auto-cancelled; the customer can pay any time before pickup. The workstation prints the receipt once it's paid in full.

The customer mail subject is 'Order #XXX has been placed' with the pickup QR.

help.panel.hq_products.subtitle: HQ / Products
help.panel.hq_products.purpose: The brand-wide product catalogue. Register products here, move them through the approval workflow, and start or stop selling them.
help.panel.hq_products.usage.1: Narrow the list with the search box and the four dropdowns (status, type, category, visibility). "Show trashed" brings soft-deleted rows back into view.
help.panel.hq_products.usage.2: Click a product name to open its detail page and edit it there. "Add product" opens a blank one.
help.panel.hq_products.usage.3: The row's "⋮" menu only offers the transitions the current status allows: Draft or Rejected → "Submit for approval"; Pending → "Approve" or "Reject"; Approved or Inactive → "Activate"; Active → "Deactivate".
help.panel.hq_products.usage.4: "Reject" needs a reason of 1–1000 characters. The confirm button stays disabled until you type one.
help.panel.hq_products.usage.5: "Export" offers four scopes: the current page, the checked rows, everything matching the filters, or every product in the brand.
help.panel.hq_products.checks.1: The status dropdown only lists Draft, Active and Inactive. Products sitting in Pending, Approved or Rejected cannot be filtered for — read the status column instead.
help.panel.hq_products.checks.2: Ticking any row replaces the search box and the filters with the bulk-action bar. Clear the selection to get them back.
help.panel.hq_products.checks.3: Changing a filter or moving to another page clears the selection. A bulk delete only ever covers rows ticked on the page you are on.
help.panel.hq_products.checks.4: The list is always sorted by last update, newest first. Clicking a column header does not sort it.
help.panel.hq_products.checks.5: Delete is a soft delete. Tick "Show trashed" to see the row again and "Restore" to bring it back.
help.panel.hq_products.checks.6: Exporting "All products" ignores both the filters and the checked rows, and writes every product.
help.panel.hq_products.glossary.tax_type: The code of the tax type assigned to the product. "—" means it has no tax type of its own and inherits the brand default.
help.panel.hq_products.glossary.variants: How many SKUs sit under the product. 0 means it has no sellable variant yet.
The share of positive reviews, with the total review count in brackets. "—" means no reviews at all — not the same as 0%.
help.panel.hq_products.glossary.status_c: Draft → Pending → Approved → Active. A rejection sends it to Rejected, from where it can be resubmitted. "Deactivate" takes Active back to Inactive.
help.panel.hq_categories.subtitle: HQ / Categories
help.panel.hq_categories.purpose: Manages the brand's product categories as a hierarchy tree. Categories are what products are filed under and what shop menus are built on.
help.panel.hq_categories.usage.1: Click the triangle to the left of a name to expand or collapse its children. Collapsed children are not rows in the table at all.
help.panel.hq_categories.usage.2: Click a category name to open its detail page and edit it there. "New" opens a create dialog.
help.panel.hq_categories.usage.3: Narrow the list with the search box, the status dropdown (All / Active / Inactive), and "Show trashed".
help.panel.hq_categories.usage.4: Delete from a row's "⋮" menu. When the category has children, the confirmation dialog tells you how many.
help.panel.hq_categories.checks.1: Deleting a parent leaves its children without one. Read the count in the confirmation dialog before confirming.
help.panel.hq_categories.checks.2: The header checkbox only selects the rows currently expanded and visible. Collapsed children are not selected.
help.panel.hq_categories.checks.3: "Export" ignores every filter and always writes the brand's complete category list to CSV.
help.panel.hq_categories.checks.4: Delete is a soft delete. Tick "Show trashed" to see the row again and "Restore" to bring it back.
help.panel.hq_categories.glossary.childr: How many descendants the category has, direct children and deeper. 0 means deleting it affects no other category.
help.panel.hq_categories.glossary.sku.de: The category's code. "—" means it has not been set, which is the same as blank.
help.panel.hq_orders.subtitle: HQ / Orders
help.panel.hq_orders.purpose: A cross-branch view of every order in the brand. Read the revenue aggregates and void an order when you have to. You cannot create or edit orders here.
help.panel.hq_orders.usage.1: Filter by status, type (dine-in / takeaway), branch, from-date and to-date. The three cards at the top summarise whatever the filters return.
help.panel.hq_orders.usage.2: Click an order number to open its detail page. From HQ the detail is read-only.
help.panel.hq_orders.usage.3: To void an order, pick "Cancel" from the row's "⋮" menu. A reason is required, up to 500 characters.
help.panel.hq_orders.checks.1: Closed, Voided and Expired orders cannot be cancelled — the menu item does not appear on those rows at all.
help.panel.hq_orders.checks.2: An order with payment already collected is refused by the server with a 409 error toast. Refund it first, then cancel.
help.panel.hq_orders.checks.3: The currency symbol on the aggregate cards is taken from the first row's order. If the filter spans branches on different currencies, the totals and the symbol disagree. Narrow to one branch before reading them.
help.panel.hq_orders.glossary.total.desc: Each row's total is shown in that order's own currency. The aggregate cards resolve their currency differently.
help.panel.hq_orders.glossary.walk_in.de: An order with no customer record attached. The name is not blank — there is no customer on the order.
help.panel.hq_orders.glossary.status_flo: Pending → Awaiting confirmation → Confirmed → Open → Dining → Checkout → Paying → Closed. Voided and Expired are terminal states that leave that chain.
help.panel.hq_customers.subtitle: HQ / Customers
help.panel.hq_customers.purpose: A read-only roll-up of every customer across the brand's branches. Check contact details and point balances, then drill into a customer.
help.panel.hq_customers.usage.1: Narrow the list with the search box and the branch filter. "Show trashed" includes soft-deleted customers.
help.panel.hq_customers.usage.2: Click a customer name, or pick "View" from the row's "⋮" menu, to open the detail page.
help.panel.hq_customers.checks.1: You cannot create, edit or delete a customer here. "View" is the only action in the row menu.
help.panel.hq_customers.checks.2: The branch filter defaults to "All branches". The branch column shows which branch each row belongs to — do not read it as the filter.
The balance computed by summing the point ledger — there is no stored balance column. 0 means no ledger entry yet, not an uncalculated value.
The branch the customer was registered at. "—" means the customer is not tied to a branch.
help.panel.hq_coupons.subtitle: HQ / Coupons
help.panel.hq_coupons.purpose: Manages the brand's discount coupons. Issue them, check their validity window and usage cap, and pause or resume them.
help.panel.hq_coupons.usage.1: Filter with the search box, the status dropdown, the branch dropdown and "Show trashed". The statuses on offer are Draft, Scheduled, Active, Paused, Expired and Exhausted.
help.panel.hq_coupons.usage.2: "New coupon" issues one. Click a code to open its detail page; edit it from the row's "⋮" menu → "Edit".
help.panel.hq_coupons.usage.3: Use "Pause" to stop a coupon being accepted and "Resume" to let it through again. Both take effect immediately.
help.panel.hq_coupons.checks.1: A coupon that has been used even once cannot be deleted — the row has neither a checkbox nor a "Delete" item. Use "Pause" instead when you want it to stop.
help.panel.hq_coupons.checks.2: The header checkbox only selects the coupons that can be deleted — unused and not already trashed. It does not select every row.
help.panel.hq_coupons.checks.3: Scheduled, Expired and Exhausted are recomputed by the server from the dates and the usage count each time. You cannot set them by hand.
help.panel.hq_coupons.glossary.usage.des: Reads "times used / cap". When no cap is set it shows "times used / ∞". The ∞ means unlimited — it is not a zero.
help.panel.hq_coupons.glossary.value.des: A percentage coupon reads like "20%", or "20% (≤ 500)" when it has a cap. A fixed-amount coupon shows the bare number with no currency symbol.
help.panel.hq_coupons.glossary.window.de: Valid-from → valid-until. A coupon outside that window reads as Scheduled or Expired even if it was activated.
help.panel.hq_payments.subtitle: HQ / Settings / Payments
help.panel.hq_payments.purpose: A single view of whether the brand's payment setup is ready to go live. Every number is a link into the screen where you fix it.
help.panel.hq_payments.usage.1: Read the "Overall readiness" badge first: Ready, Action required, or Setup required.
help.panel.hq_payments.usage.2: Click the three cards to jump to "Connections", "Shop coverage" and "Option policies" respectively.
help.panel.hq_payments.usage.3: The "Blockers" card lists whatever is holding go-live back. "Resolve" takes you straight to that item's settings screen.
help.panel.hq_payments.usage.4: The left sub-nav moves between Overview, Connections, Option policies, Shop coverage, Settlements and Tender vocabulary.
help.panel.hq_payments.checks.1: The "Blockers" card is not rendered at all when there are none. Its absence means there are no blockers, not that they are hidden.
help.panel.hq_payments.checks.2: This screen only reflects state; it changes nothing. Every fix happens on the screen the link takes you to.
help.panel.hq_payments.checks.3: The settings live at two levels: the tab strip on top spans all brand settings, the left sub-nav covers the sections inside Payments.
help.panel.hq_payments.glossary.connecti: Reads "connections able to take payment / connections registered". The denominator is every connection you have set up, the numerator how many actually work.
help.panel.hq_payments.glossary.shops.de: Reads shops that can take payment over all shops in the brand. A ready connection does not raise this number until it is assigned to shops.
How many payment options are switched on out of those defined. The three cards count different things — adding them together means nothing.
help.panel.shop_orders.subtitle: Shop / Orders
help.panel.shop_orders.purpose: The working order list for this shop. Track orders in flight, raise one at the counter, and void when you have to.
help.panel.shop_orders.usage.1: Filter by status, type (dine-in / takeaway), from-date and to-date. The search box matches order codes and customer names.
help.panel.shop_orders.usage.2: "New order" raises a counter order. Click an order code to open its detail page.
help.panel.shop_orders.usage.3: To void an order, pick "Cancel" from the row's "⋮" menu. A reason is required, up to 500 characters.
help.panel.shop_orders.checks.1: The list refreshes itself every 15 seconds. An order settled on the kiosk or the customer-facing app flips to Closed here without you refreshing.
help.panel.shop_orders.checks.2: Closed, Voided and Expired orders cannot be cancelled — the menu item does not appear on those rows at all.
help.panel.shop_orders.checks.3: An order with payment already collected is refused by the server with a 409 error toast. Refund it first, then cancel.
help.panel.shop_orders.checks.4: The cancel dialog's reason box starts empty for every order. A reason typed for one order is never carried into the next.
help.panel.shop_orders.glossary.status_f: Pending → Awaiting confirmation → Confirmed → Open → Dining → Checkout → Paying → Closed. Voided and Expired are terminal states that leave that chain.
An order with no customer record attached. The name is not blank — there is no customer on the order.
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.subtitle: Shop / Stock levels
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.purpose: A read-only view of what is on hand in this shop's warehouses. Product variants and raw materials share one table.
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.usage.1: Filter by warehouse, by stock status (In stock / Low / Out of stock), and by SKU or name in the search box.
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.usage.2: The "Type" column tells you whether the row is a sellable variant or a raw material.
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.usage.3: Nothing on this screen moves stock. Movements are made on the transactions, counts, disposals and transfers screens.
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.checks.1: A row can only read "Low" if it has a minimum stock set. With no minimum, a quantity of 1 still reads "In stock".
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.checks.2: The filters are not kept in the URL. Reloading the page resets them to their defaults.
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.checks.3: The pager only appears when the result runs to more than one page. No buttons means you are seeing everything.
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.glossary.mi: The reorder point and the ceiling. Only the minimum drives the "Low" badge; the maximum does not affect it. A row with neither set shows "—".
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.glossary.lo: The material's lot code. A "Legacy" pill on a material row means stock carried over from before lot tracking — it is untracked. Variant rows have no lot, so they read "—".
help.panel.shop_stock_levels.glossary.ty: variant is a sellable product variant; material is a raw input used in production. A row is always one or the other, never both.
help.panel.shop_till.subtitle: Shop / Cashier shifts
help.panel.shop_till.purpose: The manager's view of cash on the tills. Track which shifts are open, today's variance, and any shift left hanging.
help.panel.shop_till.usage.1: Work across the three tabs: "Overview" for the current picture, "Shift History" for past shifts, "Stale Shifts" to clear the ones left hanging.
help.panel.shop_till.usage.2: Clicking the "Stale shifts" card jumps to the "Stale Shifts" tab. The other three cards are not clickable.
help.panel.shop_till.usage.3: In "Per-till status", a till with a shift open is a link to that shift's detail page. An idle till's card is not a link.
help.panel.shop_till.usage.4: The "Variance trend" chart takes 7, 14, 30 or 90 days. It opens on 14.
help.panel.shop_till.checks.1: The screen polls every 5 seconds, but the polling stops while the browser tab is in the background. Numbers seen right after switching back may still be the pre-switch ones.
help.panel.shop_till.checks.2: While a shift is open, the shop's currency, tax-inclusive toggle and tax-rounding settings are locked. Close the shift before changing them.
help.panel.shop_till.checks.3: "Recent settlements" shows the latest 5 only. Go to the "Shift History" tab to see further back.
help.panel.shop_till.glossary.variance.d: Counted cash minus expected cash. A positive figure in green means the drawer is over; a negative one in red means it is short. 0 means they match.
help.panel.shop_till.glossary.stale.desc: A shift left unclosed. The KPI figure is Overdue plus Expired added together, and the line under it breaks out those two counts.
help.panel.shop_till.glossary.stale_band: The two warning bands on a till card. Past 24 hours open it turns amber; past 40 hours it turns red. The 40-hour badge replaces the 24-hour one rather than sitting beside it.
help.panel.shop_till.glossary.open_tills: Tills with a shift open over tills registered. The denominator is every till you have configured, not just the busy ones.
help.panel.shop_production_batches.purpo: The list of production batches that turn recipes into prepared material. Track planned versus actual yield and why they differed.
help.panel.shop_production_batches.usage: Filter by warehouse, status, from-date, to-date, and batch code in the search box.
"New batch" starts one. Click a batch code to open its detail page.
Status moves — approve, start, complete — are made on the batch's detail page, not from this list.
help.panel.shop_production_batches.check: The "Actual" column only carries a value once the batch is Completed. A "—" on any other status means the actual yield is not settled yet — it does not mean zero.
The "Variance reason" cell is clipped to one line. Hover the text to read the whole thing in a tooltip.
The filters are not kept in the URL. Reloading the page resets them to their defaults.
help.panel.shop_production_batches.gloss: Draft → Pending → Approved → In progress → Completed. Cancelled is a terminal state reachable from any stage.
How many times the recipe is being run. ×2 means the material requirement is twice what the recipe states.
Planned is the yield expected when the batch was raised; Actual is what was recorded on completion. Both use the same unit, and a gap between them is what the variance reason explains.
help.panel.shop_settings.subtitle: Shop / Settings
help.panel.shop_settings.purpose: Where this shop's operating rules are set: how orders behave, tax and currency, payment methods, and cash denominations — one tab each.
help.panel.shop_settings.usage.1: Pick your area from the tab strip: Orders, Payments, Cart Timeout, Takeaway Payment, Point earning, Denominations, Payment methods.
help.panel.shop_settings.usage.2: Change something and the "Save changes" button becomes clickable, with an unsaved marker beside it. With nothing changed it stays disabled.
help.panel.shop_settings.usage.3: Many settings offer a "use HQ" option. Picking it hands the value back to the brand default, so a later change at HQ follows through automatically.
help.panel.shop_settings.usage.4: On the "Denominations" and "Payment methods" tabs, adding, editing or deleting a row applies straight away. There is no save button on those.
help.panel.shop_settings.checks.1: Save applies only to the tab you are on. If you touched more than one tab, save each of them.
help.panel.shop_settings.checks.2: While a cashier shift is open, three settings refuse to change: currency, the tax-inclusive toggle, and tax rounding. The server rejects them with a 409 and the control snaps back. Close the till first.
help.panel.shop_settings.checks.3: The confirmation timeout takes 1–30 minutes and prep minutes per item takes 0–120. A value outside the range shows an error and disables the save button.
help.panel.shop_settings.checks.4: Rows defined organization-wide cannot be edited or deleted from this screen — those are the rows whose edit and delete buttons are greyed out.
help.panel.shop_settings.glossary.two_pa: Two different tabs with similar names. "Payments" configures the payment options this shop uses; "Payment methods" defines the tender vocabulary itself.
help.panel.shop_settings.glossary.use_hq: The setting holds no value of its own and reads the brand default instead. That is not the same as setting the same value locally — a change at HQ flows through only in the first case.
help.panel.shop_settings.glossary.tax_in: Whether product prices already contain tax. It changes how bills are computed, which is why it is locked mid-shift.
help.panel.shop_tenders.subtitle: Shop / Tender activation
help.panel.shop_tenders.purpose: Switches which tenders this shop can settle with. The organization defines the list; this screen decides which of them this shop uses.
help.panel.shop_tenders.usage.1: Flip the switch at the right of a row. There is no save button — the change is stored the moment you flip it.
help.panel.shop_tenders.usage.2: The count in the header tells you how many are active out of the total.
help.panel.shop_tenders.checks.1: A flip affects this shop only. The organization-wide definition is untouched and no other shop changes.
help.panel.shop_tenders.checks.2: You cannot add or remove a tender here. The vocabulary itself is managed on the "Payment methods" tab of the shop settings screen.
help.panel.shop_tenders.checks.3: There is no filter and no pager on this screen. What the table shows is the complete effective list for this shop.
help.panel.shop_tenders.glossary.tender_: The tender's identifier. The display name changes with the interface language; the key does not. Quote the key when raising a support request.
A row showing "← key" beside its name has that key as its parent — it tells you which tender this one derives from.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.subtitle: Shop / Dashboard
help.panel.shop_dashboard.purpose: The manager's one-screen read of today: revenue, orders, table occupancy and stock warnings. Figures use this shop's own currency.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.usage.1: The four cards on top give you today at a glance. The arrow and percentage compare against yesterday.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.usage.2: The chart covers the last 7 days. Its tabs switch between revenue and order count.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.usage.3: Below that: the table-status breakdown, top-selling items, the production queue, recent orders and branch reviews.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.checks.1: The period is fixed: the cards are today and the chart is the last 7 days. For any other range, use the date filters on the Orders screen.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.checks.2: Each section loads on its own. If one fails the rest still render, and only that section shows a retry button.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.checks.3: There is no refresh button on this screen. Reload the browser or reopen the screen to pull fresh numbers.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.glossary.delta: A green up arrow is a rise, a red down arrow a fall. The comparison is always yesterday — it cannot be switched to last week or last month.
help.panel.shop_dashboard.glossary.low_s: How many items sit below their minimum stock. An item with no minimum set never appears here.
help.panel.shop_menus.subtitle: Shop / Menus
help.panel.shop_menus.purpose: The menus handed down to this shop. HQ authors the menu itself; the shop adjusts prices and which variants are shown.
help.panel.shop_menus.usage.1: Filter with the search box and the status dropdown. Click a card to open that menu's detail page.
help.panel.shop_menus.usage.2: Prices and variant visibility are edited inside the detail page, not from this list.
help.panel.shop_menus.usage.3: When the HQ master changes, pull it in with "Sync" on the card. A confirmation dialog appears first.
help.panel.shop_menus.checks.1: You cannot create or delete a menu here. Menus are distributed by HQ.
help.panel.shop_menus.checks.2: "Sync" overwrites from the master. Adjustments made at this shop may be reverted, so read the confirmation dialog before you go ahead.
help.panel.shop_menus.checks.3: The "Sync" button only appears on menus that are linked to a master. A shop-only menu does not show it.
help.panel.shop_menus.glossary.master.de: The HQ original. Only menus linked to one can be synced; an unlinked menu stands alone and is unaffected by HQ changes.
help.panel.shop_floating_sections.purpos: The menu sections that appear only during certain hours — breakfast, lunch, late night — as they apply to this shop.
Filter with the search box and the status dropdown, then click a card to open its detail page.
The schedule and the items it covers are edited on the detail page.
When the HQ master changes, pull it in with "Sync" on the card.
help.panel.shop_floating_sections.checks: You cannot create or delete a section here — that happens at HQ.
The "Sync" button only appears on sections linked to a master.
help.panel.shop_floating_sections.glossa: The hours in which the section shows. Outside them it does not appear on the customer's screen even when it is active.
help.panel.shop_customers.subtitle: Shop / Customers
help.panel.shop_customers.purpose: This shop's customer register. Check contact details and point balances, and correct a record when you need to.
help.panel.shop_customers.usage.1: Find a customer with the search box. "Show trashed" brings soft-deleted customers back into view.
help.panel.shop_customers.usage.2: Click a customer name to open the detail page. Edit from the row's "⋮" menu → "Edit".
help.panel.shop_customers.checks.1: The HQ customer screen is read-only; this one can edit and delete. What you change here is the brand-wide customer record.
help.panel.shop_customers.checks.2: Delete is a soft delete. Tick "Show trashed" to see the row again and "Restore" to bring it back.
help.panel.shop_customers.glossary.point: The balance computed by summing the point ledger. 0 means no ledger entry yet, not an uncalculated value.
help.panel.shop_faqs.subtitle: Shop / FAQs
help.panel.shop_faqs.purpose: Manages the questions and answers customers see. Questions handed down from HQ and this shop's own sit in the same table.
help.panel.shop_faqs.usage.1: The "inherit from HQ" switch at the top decides whether HQ questions appear at this shop at all.
help.panel.shop_faqs.usage.2: The "Source" column tells you whether a row came from HQ or belongs to this shop.
help.panel.shop_faqs.usage.3: For a row from HQ, the switch in the status column controls only whether it shows at this shop.
help.panel.shop_faqs.usage.4: For the shop's own questions, the row's "⋮" menu offers edit, publish or hide, pin or unpin, and delete.
help.panel.shop_faqs.checks.1: When HQ unpublishes a question, the shop's switch is locked. Turning it on would not show the question to customers, so the control is disabled on purpose.
help.panel.shop_faqs.checks.2: Rows from HQ have no action menu — a "—" sits where the "⋮" would be. Edit those at HQ instead.
help.panel.shop_faqs.checks.3: Turning "inherit from HQ" off removes every HQ question from this shop's customer screen at once. It outranks the per-row switches.
A question written at HQ and pushed to the whole brand. The wording cannot be changed here — only whether it shows.
help.panel.shop_faqs.glossary.pin.desc: A pinned question sits at the top of the list. It is separate from publish state — pinning something unpublished still shows it to nobody.
help.panel.shop_promotions.subtitle: Shop / Promotions
help.panel.shop_promotions.purpose: Manages this shop's discount campaigns: the percentage, what it applies to, the window, and whether it is on.
help.panel.shop_promotions.usage.1: Filter by status and by "currently running". The search box matches the name.
help.panel.shop_promotions.usage.2: Create with "New", and click a name to open its detail page.
help.panel.shop_promotions.usage.3: The row's "⋮" menu switches a promotion on or off and deletes it.
help.panel.shop_promotions.checks.1: The status filter and the "currently running" filter are not the same thing. An enabled promotion outside its window is not currently running.
help.panel.shop_promotions.checks.2: Delete is a soft delete. Tick "Show trashed" to see the row again and "Restore" to bring it back.
help.panel.shop_promotions.glossary.disc: Percentage only — it reads like "−10%". A fixed-amount discount cannot be created on this screen.
help.panel.shop_promotions.glossary.scop: What the discount lands on. Two broad promotions can overlap on one bill, so check the existing ones before adding a window.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.subtitle: Shop / Point rewards
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.purpose: The rewards customers can spend points on. The brand decides what they are; this shop only decides whether it offers them.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.usage.1: Review the rewards on the "Catalog" tab and use the switch at the right to turn each one on for this shop.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.usage.2: The "Redemptions" tab shows the record of rewards actually exchanged.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.checks.1: The point cost, the image and the stock are brand-level settings. You cannot change them from this screen.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.checks.2: When HQ disables a reward the switch is locked and the row is dimmed. Flipping it would not show the reward to customers, so the control is disabled on purpose.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.checks.3: The redemption log is brand-wide. Redemptions are not tied to a branch, so exchanges made elsewhere appear here too.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.glossary.s: The units left. "Unlimited" means no cap was set — that is not the same as 0. When it runs out the cell turns into a red badge.
help.panel.shop_point_rewards.glossary.a: Whether this shop accepts the exchange. It only means anything for a reward the brand has enabled.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.subtitle: Shop / Material lots
help.panel.shop_material_lots.purpose: The material lots received at this shop. Track what is left and when it expires; this is where traceability starts.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.usage.1: Filter with the search box and the status dropdown: active, quarantined, depleted, expired, disposed.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.usage.2: "Receive" registers a new lot. Click a lot code to open its detail page.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.checks.1: The row number restarts at 1 on every page. The first row of page 2 also reads 1, so do not use it as a running count.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.checks.2: There are no per-row actions on this screen. Open the detail page to act on a lot.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.checks.3: There is no refresh button. If a fresh receipt does not show, reopen the screen.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.glossary.q: A lot held back from use, typically pending inspection. It still exists as stock but is kept out of allocation.
help.panel.shop_material_lots.glossary.d: A lot whose quantity reached 0. Unlike expired or disposed, it means the lot was consumed normally.
help.panel.shop_stock_transactions.purpo: The record of stock coming in and going out. Entries are raised here and hit the stock figures once approved.
help.panel.shop_stock_transactions.usage: Filter by warehouse, by type (stock in / stock out), by status, and by date. Status accepts more than one value.
Raise an entry with the green stock-in button or the orange stock-out button. The colours match the two types.
Click a code to open the detail page. Status moves such as approval happen there, not in this list.
help.panel.shop_stock_transactions.check: Only completed transactions move the stock figures. A draft or pending row has not changed anything on the stock screen yet.
The filters are not kept in the URL. Reloading the page resets them to their defaults.
help.panel.shop_stock_transactions.gloss: Draft → Pending → Approved → Completed. Cancelled is a terminal state reachable from any stage.
How many item lines the transaction carries. It is not the sum of the quantities.
help.panel.shop_stock_transfers.subtitle: Shop / Stock transfers
help.panel.shop_stock_transfers.purpose: The transfer notes that move stock between warehouses. Name a source and a destination, and track what is in transit.
help.panel.shop_stock_transfers.usage.1: Filter by source warehouse, destination warehouse, status and date. The two warehouses are separate dropdowns.
help.panel.shop_stock_transfers.usage.2: Raise a note with "New". Click a code to open its detail page.
help.panel.shop_stock_transfers.checks.1: Stock in transit has already left the source but has not landed at the destination. Adding up both warehouses will not account for it.
help.panel.shop_stock_transfers.checks.2: The filters are not kept in the URL. Reloading the page resets them to their defaults.
help.panel.shop_stock_transfers.glossary: Draft → Pending → Approved → In transit → Completed. In transit is a state only transfers ever reach.
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.subtitle: Shop / Stock counts
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.purpose: Manages physical stock counts. Reconcile what you counted against what the books say, then post the difference.
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.usage.1: Filter by warehouse, by scope (full or partial), and by status. Status accepts more than one value.
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.usage.2: Raise a count with "New". The create button stays disabled until a warehouse is picked.
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.usage.3: Click a code to open the detail page, and enter the counted quantities there.
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.checks.1: Stock moving in or out of the same warehouse mid-count will pull the counted and book figures apart. Freeze that warehouse while a count runs.
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.checks.2: The filters are not kept in the URL. Reloading the page resets them to their defaults.
help.panel.shop_stock_counts.glossary.sc: A full count covers every item in the warehouse; a partial count covers only the items you picked. Items left out of a partial count keep their existing figures.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.subtitle: Shop / Disposals
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.purpose: Manages disposal notes. Record what was thrown away and, once approved, take it off stock.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.usage.1: Filter by warehouse, status, date and the search box.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.usage.2: Raise a note with "New"; the waste report button opens the summary view.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.usage.3: The row's "⋮" menu only offers what the status allows: Draft → submit; Pending → approve.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.checks.1: Only draft and cancelled notes can be deleted. Pending, approved and completed notes stay on the record.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.checks.2: Cancel is only available on draft and pending notes. An approved note cannot be taken back.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.checks.3: Submit, approve and cancel are confirmed through the browser's own dialog, which looks different from the app's other dialogs.
help.panel.shop_stock_disposals.glossary: Draft → Pending → Approved → Completed. Stock only comes off for a completed note.
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.subtitle: Shop / Stock alerts
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.purpose: Lists the items that fell below their minimum and the ones that ran out. Thresholds can be corrected without leaving the screen.
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.usage.1: The three cards on top give the overall counts. Narrow the list below by warehouse, alert type and status.
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.usage.2: Open "Configure threshold" from a row to change that item's minimum stock in place.
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.checks.1: The three cards do not follow the filters. Narrowing by warehouse or type leaves the card figures at the shop-wide totals.
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.checks.2: Saving a threshold can resolve the alert on the spot, and the row then leaves the active list. A row disappearing is the fix working, not a failure.
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.glossary.al: Low stock means the quantity fell below the minimum; out of stock means it hit 0. The two do not overlap, so adding them double-counts nothing.
help.panel.shop_stock_alerts.glossary.re: An alert that no longer holds, either because stock was replenished or because the threshold was lowered. The default filter hides these.
help.panel.shop_tables.subtitle: Shop / Tables
help.panel.shop_tables.purpose: The floor plan. Table cards sit under their zone; check status and issue QR codes from here.
help.panel.shop_tables.usage.1: Create a zone with "New zone", then add tables into it with "New table".
help.panel.shop_tables.usage.2: Click the status badge on a card to change that table's state directly.
help.panel.shop_tables.usage.3: A card's "⋮" menu enlarges the QR, switches the table on or off, and reissues the QR.
help.panel.shop_tables.usage.4: "Print QR posters" outputs several tables at once. It stays disabled while there are no tables.
help.panel.shop_tables.checks.1: A table copied from the HQ default layout cannot be deleted — the delete item does not appear in its menu at all.
help.panel.shop_tables.checks.2: Editing an HQ table is only possible while the brand's allow-shop-edit switch is on.
help.panel.shop_tables.checks.3: "New table" stays disabled until at least one zone exists. Create a zone first.
help.panel.shop_tables.checks.4: After reissuing a QR, reprint that table's poster — the printed copy in the room no longer matches.
help.panel.shop_tables.glossary.hq_badge: A table copied from the brand's default layout. It can never be deleted, and whether it can be edited depends on a brand switch.
help.panel.shop_tables.glossary.inactive: Its card renders dimmed. It is not deleted — the seat still exists — but it drops out of the customer screen and of seating.
help.panel.shop_devices.subtitle: Shop / Devices
help.panel.shop_devices.purpose: Registers this shop's devices, issues pairing codes and manages their connection — POS, kiosk, KDS, handy terminals and the rest.
help.panel.shop_devices.usage.1: "Create" registers a device. A freshly registered device starts in "Pending activation".
help.panel.shop_devices.usage.2: Click the code in the "Pairing" column to see the 6-character code enlarged. Copy it with the copy button and type it into the device.
help.panel.shop_devices.usage.3: When a code expires, issue a new one from the row's "⋮" menu → regenerate code.
help.panel.shop_devices.usage.4: Detach a device with "⋮" → revoke. Clicking the device name opens the edit dialog.
help.panel.shop_devices.checks.1: The pairing dialog shows a text code only. The button carries a QR icon, but no scannable code is displayed — type it into the device by hand.
help.panel.shop_devices.checks.2: A code only shows for a device pending activation. A connected device reads "paired" instead.
help.panel.shop_devices.checks.3: Revoking cuts the device off; using it again means going through pairing from the start.
help.panel.shop_devices.checks.4: The list is always sorted by registration date, newest first. Clicking a column header does not sort it.
help.panel.shop_devices.glossary.last_se: When the device last reached the server. "—" means it has never connected — that is different from a device that lost its connection.
help.panel.shop_devices.glossary.status_: Four: pending activation, active, inactive, revoked. Revoked is what a revoke leaves behind, and is not the same as inactive.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.subtitle: Shop / Peripherals
help.panel.shop_peripherals.purpose: Registers the hardware hanging off the till — payment terminals, coin changers, printers. LAN-connected units carry their address here.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.usage.1: "Register" adds a device. Clicking a device name opens the edit dialog.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.usage.2: Filter by type. Only payment terminals and coin changers carry an address and an accepted-denominations list.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.checks.1: A payment terminal or coin changer with no host shows a red warning in the address column. That unit cannot be reached.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.checks.2: A "—" in the address and accepted columns on a printer row is normal — those two columns only apply to LAN devices.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.checks.3: The accepted column shows the first entry only and folds the rest into "+N". Hover the text to see the full list.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.glossary.net: Payment terminals and coin changers, and nothing else. They require a host; on other types a host is not used.
help.panel.shop_peripherals.glossary.acc: The denominations the unit takes. On a coin changer, picking the model can prefill this automatically.
help.panel.shop_printers.subtitle: Shop / Printers
help.panel.shop_printers.purpose: Registers this shop's printers and assigns, by role, which slips each one prints.
help.panel.shop_printers.usage.1: "Add" registers a printer. Clicking a printer name opens the edit dialog.
help.panel.shop_printers.usage.2: Use the role filter to narrow to the kitchen, bar, hall or receipt printers.
help.panel.shop_printers.checks.1: One printer can hold several roles. Several tags in the role column means exactly that — it is not a duplicate registration.
help.panel.shop_printers.checks.2: A printer with "—" in the role column prints nothing automatically. Registering it is not enough — assign a role.
help.panel.shop_printers.checks.3: "Never seen" means the printer has not reached the server yet. Even with the settings right, check the cabling and power.
Four: kitchen, bar, hall and receipt. Roles decide the routing of a slip, which is separate from the model or where the unit stands.
help.panel.shop_printers.glossary.connec: Network or USB. It shows in small type under the address, and on a network printer the address above it is the IP.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.subtitle: Shop / Print templates
help.panel.shop_print_templates.purpose: Shows which parts of each slip layout this shop overrides. The brand decides how much a shop is allowed to change.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.usage.1: The "Overrides" column spells out which paths this shop actually changes.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.usage.2: Click a template name or press "Edit" to open that layout's editor.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.usage.3: The "In force" column tells you whether what actually prints is the system default, the brand version, or the shop override.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.checks.1: An amber warning on a row means the shop has a saved override that currently changes nothing: the brand narrowed what it delegates, so the setting no longer takes effect.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.checks.2: A row reading "locked by the brand" cannot be changed from this shop.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.checks.3: If an override seems to have vanished, read the allow-list column first. The setting may still be stored — the brand may simply have withdrawn permission.
help.panel.shop_print_templates.glossary: Shows the brand version alongside the shop override version. A "—" means no version is stored at that layer.
How many paths the brand delegates to the shop. When it shrinks, an override that falls outside stays stored but stops taking effect.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.subtitle: Shop / Print jobs
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.purpose: The ledger of every slip this shop tried to print. When paper does not come out, this is the first screen to open: find the cause and close the line.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.usage.1: The summary strip at the top shows the ageing backlog and any silent printers. Clicking an entry filters the list to that status.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.usage.2: The filter button reveals the filter row. Status and kind both accept more than one value.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.usage.3: Click a row to open the detail page and record how the line was settled.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.checks.1: This screen is a ledger, not a retry console. All you can do here is write down how it was resolved — nothing on it puts paper out again.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.checks.2: Receipts, payment receipts and debt slips are never auto-resent by any machine: a slip whose acknowledgement was lost looks identical to one that printed, and guessing wrong puts two originals into the world.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.checks.3: The date filters use the branch's business day, not the viewer's. Looking in from another city still lines up with the shop's own day.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.glossary.conf: Separates "the paper came out" from "the bytes left". On a raw socket the system only knows the data was sent. It sits beside the status in a different colour.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.glossary.queu: Who is responsible for retrying that job. A slip going through the workstation is retried by the workstation itself, so the cloud side has no way to resend it.
help.panel.shop_print_jobs.glossary.need: A job that will not settle on its own and needs a human decision to close. It is the reason this screen exists, and it is tracked apart from plain failure.
help.panel.shop_production_orders.purpos: The production orders that turn recipes into finished goods. Reconcile planned quantity against what was actually made.
Filter by warehouse and status. The statuses are draft, pending, approved, in progress, completed and cancelled.
Raise an order with "New". Click a code to open the detail page and move the status forward there.
help.panel.shop_production_orders.checks: The "Actual" column only carries a value once the order is completed. A "—" on any other status means the actual is not settled yet — not zero.
The filters are not kept in the URL. Reloading the page resets them to their defaults.
help.panel.shop_production_orders.glossa: A production order makes a finished good; a batch preps raw material. They count in different units, so adding the two together means nothing.
The product variant the order produces. Only variants that have a recipe can be chosen.
help.panel.shop_production_calculator.pu: Works out how many units you can make from current stock, and names the ingredient holding you back.
help.panel.shop_production_calculator.us: Pick one warehouse and at least one variant, then press "Calculate". The button stays disabled until both are set.
The result shows, per variant, how many are producible and which ingredient caps that number.
Enter a desired quantity to run it backwards and get the list of what is short for that number. The seed button fills in the producible figure.
Pressing "Create an order for this variant" opens the production-order form with the warehouse and quantity already filled in.
help.panel.shop_production_calculator.ch: When the amber shared-ingredients warning appears, the producible figures cannot all be achieved at once: they compete for the same material, so making one lowers the other.
The reverse calculation does nothing unless the quantity is greater than 0. If pressing it seems to have no effect, check the number in the box.
Only variants that have a recipe can be picked. If the product you want is missing, register its recipe first.
The calculation looks only at the warehouse you picked. Stock sitting in another warehouse does not count towards the figure.
help.panel.shop_production_calculator.gl: The most you can make from that warehouse alone. Green means at least one; red is 0, meaning an ingredient has run out.
The ingredient that sets the producible figure. Replenishing that one raises the number; topping up anything else will not move it.
More than one variant drawing on the same material. Each producible figure assumes the others are not made, so they cannot simply be added up.
help.panel.shop_warehouses.subtitle: Shop / Warehouses
help.panel.shop_warehouses.purpose: Registers the places stock lives. Warehouses are the unit every stock, transfer, count and production screen works in.
help.panel.shop_warehouses.usage.1: Filter by type, branch and status. The status dropdown includes a "deleted" option.
help.panel.shop_warehouses.usage.2: Create with "New". The row's "⋮" menu switches a warehouse on or off, deletes it, and restores it.
help.panel.shop_warehouses.checks.1: Deactivating a warehouse takes it out of the dropdowns on new transactions. Stock already sitting in it does not disappear.
help.panel.shop_warehouses.checks.2: Deleting a warehouse that still holds stock hides that stock from every screen. Empty it with a transfer or a count first.
help.panel.shop_warehouses.glossary.type: Three: main, branch and production. A production warehouse carries prep movements and is counted apart from sellable stock.
help.panel.shop_warehouses.glossary.memb: How many people can work the warehouse. A 0 does not stop it working — it just means nobody has been assigned.
help.panel.shop_notifications_audit.purp: The record of notifications raised at this shop — what went out and when.
help.panel.shop_notifications_audit.usag: The priority buttons at the top narrow the log. The pressed one shows as filled.
Each row carries the priority, the event type and the time it happened.
help.panel.shop_notifications_audit.chec: This screen only reads the record. You cannot send, resend or delete a notification from it.
There is no search box and no date filter. Priority is the only axis you can narrow on.
help.panel.shop_notifications_audit.glos: An identifier such as `stock.alert.low`. It is the same string the routing screen uses, so you can copy one from here when writing a rule.
Defines the groups a notification goes to. Conditions such as role are written as a rule and used as the target of a broadcast.
"Create" asks for a name, a description and a rule. The rule is written as JSON.
The prefilled rule doubles as the template — start by changing the role in it.
An audience cannot be edited once created. To change the conditions, create a new one and delete the old.
A malformed rule will not save and shows an error in place. Check the brackets and the quotes.
Deleting an audience takes away the target of any broadcast that pointed at it. Check whether it is in use first.
How the conditions in the rule join. `or` matches anyone meeting one of them; `and` matches only those meeting all. The default is `or`, so narrowing means changing it.
Defines the wording of a notification. A broadcast picks one of these templates to send.
"Create" asks for a key and the content. The key is an identifier such as `stock.alert.low`.
The content is entered as JSON, and the prefilled value doubles as the template.
A template cannot be edited once created. To change the wording, create a new one and delete the old.
Malformed JSON will not save and shows an error in place.
Deleting a template takes away the wording from any broadcast that used it. Check whether it is in use first.
The string that identifies the template. It is written the same way as a routing event type, but the two are separate and need not match.
help.panel.shop_notifications_routing.pu: Overrides which channels carry each event. An event with no row here falls back to the default configuration.
help.panel.shop_notifications_routing.us: Type an event type in the card at the top, flip the channel switches, and press save to add an override row.
Flipping a switch on an existing row saves it immediately. There is no per-row save button.
help.panel.shop_notifications_routing.ch: The bin button on a row deletes it immediately, with no confirmation. Check which row you are on before pressing it.
An event type may contain only lower-case letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens. Capitals or spaces stop it saving.
Deleting a row returns that event to the default channels. It does not stop the notification.
help.panel.shop_notifications_routing.gl: Four: in-app, realtime, email and push. Several can run at once, and then the same notification arrives once per channel.
help.panel.shop_notifications_compose.pu: Picks an audience and a template and sends the notification to everyone in it. Sending happens straight away.
help.panel.shop_notifications_compose.us: Pick an audience. Only the ones created on the Audiences screen appear here.
Pick a template. Only the ones created on the Templates screen appear here.
Choose the channels and the priority. A filled channel button is on, and only in-app starts switched on.
help.panel.shop_notifications_compose.ch: Pressing send broadcasts on the spot — there is no confirmation step and no preview. Re-read the audience and the template before you press it.
A sent notification cannot be recalled. There is no undo on this screen.
Trying to send with no channel selected raises an error, as does leaving the audience or the template unset.
help.panel.shop_notifications_compose.gl: Four steps: low, normal, high, urgent. Which channels carry it is set by the channel buttons, so raising the priority does not add a channel.
The notification that lands on the bell in the admin UI. It is the only channel on by default — email and push must be picked deliberately.
shop.menu.schedules.campaign_window_hint: Leave empty for no date limit. Outside the window the menu is hidden everywhere — POS, customer screens and the offline LAN till.
shop.menu.schedules.date_range_invalid: End date cannot be before the start date.
hq.menus.schedules.recurrence_hint: One kind per row. To use both — say the 1st and 15th of every month plus a one-off on 20 Aug — add two schedules; a menu's schedules add up.
hq.menus.schedules.days_of_month_hint: The selected days repeat every month. The 31st simply does not occur in a 30-day month — it does not slide to the last day.
hq.menus.schedules.specific_dates_hint: Only the dates listed here, and they do not repeat. Click a date to remove it.
shop_debts.title: Customer debt
shop_debts.subtitle: Money this shop is owed, split by how it arose.
shop_debts.why_separate: These two are deliberately not added together. An on-account balance is a decision — you agreed to extend credit. A part-paid order is an incident — nobody closed it. They need different action, and merging them hides the second inside the first.
shop_debts.on_account.title: On-account balance
shop_debts.on_account.desc: Credit granted on purpose, charged to a customer account.
shop_debts.on_account.empty: No customer carries an on-account balance.
shop_debts.part_paid.title: Part-paid orders
shop_debts.part_paid.desc: The customer paid some and left. No debt report can see this — it lives on the order, not on a payment.
hq.transactions.title: Transaction lookup
hq.transactions.description: Search by transaction date, amount and counterparty (JP e-book preservation search requirements)
hq.transactions.referencePlaceholder: Reference — payment ID, gateway intent ID, or the cash recycler's transaction number
hq.brand.settings.cash_variance.section_: The book, the machine's counted cash and the human count are compared at shift close; only variances above this amount raise an alert. The right value depends on how much a shop takes, so it is set per brand.
hq.brand.settings.cash_variance.zero_hin: 0 is a valid setting — it means "alert on every variance".
hq.brand.settings.cash_variance.range_er: Enter a whole number between 0 and 1,000,000.
